scenes.title: Cardiac arrest in brief
scenes.narration: Cardiac arrest in brief. Each heartbeat starts as an electrical impulse; in cardiac arrest the heart stops beating effectively.
In ventricular fibrillation the ventricles quiver. The right ventricle and the left ventricle eject no blood, so the aorta carries nothing. Chest compressions push blood out of the heart again.

scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[Recognition] --> B[Compressions] --> C[Defibrillation] --> D[Advanced care]
scenes.narration: Survival depends on a chain. Recognition comes first. Compressions keep blood moving. Defibrillation restores a rhythm. Advanced care follows.
Survival to discharge is low. Out of hospital it is about 10.5%. In hospital, for adults, it is about 23.6%.
To summarise: cardiac arrest is electrical, compressions move the blood, and the chain starts with recognition.
